title: Node/Room Rendering Implementation Plan

notes: Inspired by the modular-spaceship-simulator structural graph (keel, ribs, beams) and its SDF skinning pipeline.
This plan reuses the same dependency map idea to build rooms/nodes as framed structural volumes before skinning.

sourceInspiration.name: modular-spaceship-simulator
sourceInspiration.description: Ship shells are driven by a StructuralGraph (Keel, Ribs, HullSections) and a StructuralGenerator that spits out capsules and spheres (beams and ribs) before the shader looms the skin with SDF unions.

dependencyMap.Keel: central spine that anchors every node/room along the vertical stack; defines t-coordinates for frames.
dependencyMap.Ribs: planar cross-sections placed along the keel; supply profile, scale, and adjacency references for floors and beams.
dependencyMap.Beams: capsule primitives (or in our case wing plates) that span between ribs and create frame connections for shared walls.
dependencyMap.Hull Sections / Skin: a lofted, parametric outer shell that blends between ribs; the shader in the example performs smooth union SDFs to form the skin over the frame.
dependencyMap.Modules (rooms): sub-assemblies defined in DNA that carve out pressurized spaces via capsules and boxes/lights.

axiomatic: Rooms are the boolean intersections of floors, ceilings, and walls; structure defines these constraints.
Structure (beams/pillars) dictates the boundaries and the skin is procedural.
axiological: Procedural emergence over prefab: adjacent rooms automatically merge shared walls via frame connectivity.
Structural honesty: visualization should directly reflect the load-bearing graph inherited from keel-beam-rib topology.
teleological: Create a living simulation where structural input reconfigures the rendered shell and all rooms/nodes remain perfectly batched and infinitely scalable.

scope: Adapt the spaceship StructuralGraph (Keel + Ribs + Beams) into a tower node graph (foundation + vertical spine + floor plates).
Drive room generation via that graph so shared walls collapse naturally when nodes touch.
Render wall skins as procedural SDFs or batched meshes derived from the frame data.
Expose adjacency metadata for future procedural placement across rooms/corridors.

workstreams.name: Structural Node Graph (Keel + Ribs)
goals: Model each node/room as a slice along a keel with rib references (similar to ship ribs).
Define core beams that connect ribs, representing vertical/horizontal edges of rooms.
Store metadata for floors, ceilings, and wall boundaries derived from turned frames.

phases.name: Node spine ingestion
tasks: Introduce a keel-like vertical spline that indexes every level.
Align rib slices to that spline, deriving width/depth/height per node.
Record structural adjacency so a downstream beam builder knows which neighbors share walls.

phases.name: Beam & rib metadata
tasks: Generate beam primitive definitions (capsules/boxes) spanning adjacent ribs.
Tag each beam with its role (wall, floor, ceiling, column).
Keep material/skin hints so later shaders can highlight load-bearing elements.

criteria: Every node references a keel position and rib pair.
Beams share endpoints when rooms are adjacent, enabling automatic wall merging.
Adjacency metadata is serializable and queryable via the node graph.

workstreams.name: Frame and Wall Generation (Beams → Inner/Outer Walls)
goals: Render the frame using capsule/box primitives derived from the node graph.
Build inner shell (interior walls, floors) and outer shell (exterior walls, facade).
Ensure beams behave like ribs from the spaceship shader—they define where the skin must attach.

phases.name: Beam instancing
tasks: Convert beam definitions into instanced SDF primitives or batched meshes.
Support toggling visibility per beam role (load-bearing vs partition).
Prepare uniform data for the skin shader to know where beam endpoints reside.

phases.name: Inner/outer shell tessellation
tasks: Loft hull surfaces akin to the spaceship shader’s rib lofts using the beam/rib outlines.
Create separate geometries for inner (interior) and outer (exterior) skins.
Keep wall thicknesses deterministic from the structural inputs and allow cutaways to reveal interiors.

criteria: Beam instancing data references actual keel/rib endpoints.
Inner and outer shells render in sequence so beam outlines align to procedural surfaces.
The skin generation works even when adjacent nodes share beams, preventing double-walls.

workstreams.name: Skin & Node Visualization (SDF, Materials, Selection)
goals: Leverage shader-driven SDF unions (as in shaderCompiler.ts) to produce smooth skins over the frame.
Attach materials to show structural honesty (steel beams, glass inner walls).
Link selection/cutaway layers to the structural metadata rather than raw mesh offsets.

phases.name: Materialized SDF pipeline
tasks: Compile shader snippets using beam/node data (capsules, boxes, rounding) to match rooms' structural roles.
Add glow/selection layers similar to the spaceship numeric IDs (1.0 for beams, 2.0 for skin).
Expose shader constants for wall thickness, adjacency, and cutaway clipping.

phases.name: Selection & adjacency overlays
tasks: Bind the selection indicator to canonical structural faces (top/ceiling, bottom/floor) derived from adjacency data.
Render adjacency metadata (shared walls) so procedural furniture can query safe placement zones.
Keep cutaway logic non-destructive so structural data remains authoritative.

criteria: Shader pipeline renders room skins with beam highlights and clean cutaways.
Selection aligns to the true structural front face and respects adjacency (shared wall merging).
Adjacency data surfaces placement zones for future object generation.

qualityGuards: No manual wall duplication—shared beams should be reconciled via adjacency metadata.
Keep shaders deterministic; identical structural graphs produce byte-identical SDFs.
Use feature-sliced modules: graph modeling, frame generation, skinning, overlays.
Never mutate structural intent during cutaways or selection highlighting.
definitionOfDone: Nodes/rooms rendered from the keel/rib/beam dependency map aligned with rooms-source-of-truth intents.
Adjacent rooms share walls automatically without duplicate geometry.
Selection and cutaway layers pull from structural metadata, not ad hoc offsets.
Completion checks above report `complete` once each section is validated.
